name: Al Hoceima
hero_subtitle: Where the Rif meets the Mediterranean: cliff-backed coves, Quemado Beach, a national park of sea and mountains, and a calm northern bay.

info.best_time_val: May – October for beaches; spring & autumn for hiking
info.vibe_val: Mediterranean bay, dramatic cliffs, relaxed Rif coast

overview.title: Welcome to Al Hoceima — bay, cliffs, and Mediterranean light
overview.p1: Al Hoceima sits on a wide natural bay on Morocco’s Mediterranean shore, framed by the Rif mountains and the protected coastline of Al Hoceima National Park. The city itself is relaxed and authentic; the main draw is the water — golden urban beaches, jewel-like coves, and boat-only inlets beneath high limestone cliffs.
overview.p2: Travellers come for Quemado and Sfiha, for Cala Bonita and Cala Iris, for scenic park trails, and short boat trips along the cliffs. A three to five-day stay leaves plenty of room for beach relaxation, park explorations, and slow evenings along the corniche.
overview.p3: Unlike the Atlantic cities further south, the sea here is typically calmer, the light sharper, and the rhythm distinctly local. It is one of Morocco’s quietest Mediterranean escapes — ideal if you want coastline and nature without the crowds.

places.title: Must-visit places in Al Hoceima
places.subtitle: Beaches, national park, coves, and the bustling fishing port.

quemado.title: Quemado Beach
quemado.desc: The city’s iconic main beach — golden sand, clear waters, and easy access from the town centre.

parc_national.title: Al Hoceima National Park
parc_national.desc: Dramatic coastal cliffs, marine reserve, and hiking trails where the Rif mountains drop into the Mediterranean.

cala_bonita.title: Cala Bonita
cala_bonita.desc: A sheltered jewel cove close to town, popular for swimming and crystal-clear water.

sfiha.title: Sfiha Beach
sfiha.desc: Soft sand and family-friendly swimming conditions just a short drive from the centre.

port_corniche.title: Port & Corniche
port_corniche.desc: Working fishing harbour, evening promenade, and the daily heartbeat of the bay.

cala_iris.title: Cala Iris
cala_iris.desc: Charming fishing village and gateway cove along the national park shoreline.

torres_alcala.title: Torres de Alcalá
torres_alcala.desc: Historic coastal watchtowers and scenic walks with open views across park cliffs and sea.

bades.title: Bades Bay
bades.desc: A wide sweep of peaceful beach near historic Badis, with boat trips and magnificent scenery.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day plan for Al Hoceima
itinerary.subtitle: Bay beaches first, then park coast, followed by a flexible day for coves or rest.

day1.title: Town & Quemado
day1.desc: Explore the corniche and port, then head to Quemado or Sfiha for a swim and sunset.

day2.title: National Park & Cala Iris
day2.desc: Take a boat or drive into the park — cliffs, Cala Iris, and optional Torres de Alcalá.

day3.title: Coves or Bades
day3.desc: Relax at Cala Bonita, venture to Bades Bay, or take a second park excursion.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Stroll along the harbour and seafront promenade to get your bearings on the bay.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Enjoy your first swim on the main city beaches, with nearby cafés for shade and refreshments.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Savour fresh grilled fish at the port and enjoy a peaceful end to your first day.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Drive or take an organised trip along the scenic national park coastline.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Enjoy short coastal walks, panoramas from Torres de Alcalá, or a boat section along the cliffs.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Relax with a simple dinner in town and rest up for another day of exploration.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Swim in a sheltered cove or head west for a wide bay day at Bades.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Visit a second beach, take a gentle walk, or relax before your departure.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Enjoy a final evening stroll along the corniche or a quiet dinner.

directory.title: Find your ideal stay in Al Hoceima
directory.subtitle: Hotels near Quemado, accommodation along the corniche, and options toward the park coast.

eat.title: Where to eat in Al Hoceima
eat.subtitle: Fresh seafood, simple port eateries, and scenic corniche cafés.

roudani.title: Port-side grills
roudani.desc: Fresh seafood grills right near the harbour as the fishing boats return.

maryam.title: Corniche cafés
maryam.desc: Mint tea, fresh juice, and sunset views overlooking the bay.

zitoune.title: Simple local tables
zitoune.desc: Authentic, everyday Moroccan dishes away from the main beach strip.

nomad.title: Hotel restaurants
nomad.desc: Reliable dining options for hotel guests and visitors.

jardin.title: Town seafood
jardin.desc: Fresh fish platters and salads in the centre between beach sessions.

fassia.title: Town café stop
fassia.desc: A great spot for coffee and a peaceful pause while exploring town.

moha.title: Beach snacks
moha.desc: Light bites and refreshments near the main beach during the summer season.

bacha.title: Neighbourhood eateries
bacha.desc: Quiet, traditional spots preferred by local residents.

elfenn.title: Evening fish dining
elfenn.desc: Atmospheric evening dining near the water as the corniche fills up.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: The town is compact; main beaches are short taxi rides. Reaching national park coves usually requires a car, organized tour, or boat. Always agree on taxi prices in advance.

bargain.title: Sun & sea
bargain.desc: The Mediterranean sun is strong in summer. Pack high SPF sunscreen, water, and shade. Check sea conditions before booking park boat excursions.

water.title: Cash & seasons
water.desc: Carry cash (MAD) for taxis and small vendors. Peak beach season is summer, while spring and autumn offer milder weather and quieter hiking trails.

daytrips.title: Best outings from Al Hoceima
daytrips.subtitle: National park shoreline, hidden coves, and the wider Rif coast.

national_park.title: National Park boat or trail
national_park.desc: Half-day trip to sea cliffs and hidden coves by boat or guided coastal trek.

cala_iris_torres.title: Cala Iris & Torres de Alcalá
cala_iris_torres.desc: A scenic park-coast village, historical towers, and sweeping Mediterranean views.

bades_bay.title: Bades Bay
bades_bay.desc: A wide beach day west of town with options for boat trips around the rocky islets.

rif_hinterland.title: Rif foothill villages
rif_hinterland.desc: A short inland drive for local weekly markets and fresh mountain air.

q1.question: How many days should I stay in Al Hoceima?
q1.answer: Three days are ideal to cover the main city beaches and one park outing. Five days allow for a more relaxed pace, including trips to Cala Iris, Torres de Alcalá, and Bades Bay.

q2.question: Is Al Hoceima only for beach holidays?
q2.answer: While beaches are the highlight, the national park, cliff walks, fresh seafood scene, and Rif mountain hinterland offer plenty of nature and culture.

q3.question: How do I get to Al Hoceima?
q3.answer: You can fly directly to Cherif Al Idrissi Airport (AHU) from major Moroccan cities, or take a scenic drive through the Rif mountains from Tetouan, Chefchaouen, or Fez.

q4.question: When is the best time to visit?
q4.answer: May to October is best for swimming and warm beach days. Spring and autumn are excellent for hiking, clear views, and avoiding summer crowds.
